examples.en: That comedian's facial expressions are really funny.
When I was little, my dream was to be a comedian.
The comedian sang a song on the broadcast.

examples.ko: 저는 개그우먼 한 분을 아주 좋아해요.
examples.en: I really like one of the comedians.
I took a photo with my comedian friend.
People lined up to see the comedian.

explain: 남자는 '개그맨', 여자는 '개그우먼'이라고 해요. 성별 없이 부를 때는 '코미디언'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: That male comedian's facial expressions are really funny.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남자 코미디언을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a male comedian.

phrases.example: 제 꿈은 유명한 코미디언이 되는 거예요.
phrases.en: My dream is to become a famous comedian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성별 없이 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word usable regardless of gender.

phrases.en: My older sister practices to become a comedienne.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about dreams or jobs.

explain_en: A male one is a 개그맨 and a female one is a 개그우먼. To refer to either without gender, people also say 코미디언.

examples.en: This school has an excellent faculty.

examples.ko: 새 학기에 교수진이 몇 명 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: A few members of the faculty changed this semester.

examples.ko: 학교 홈페이지에서 교수진 소개를 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I read the faculty introduction on the school website.

examples.ko: 외국인 교수진이 많은 학교를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a school with many foreign faculty.
The faculty and students had lunch together.
The department faculty's research fields are varied.

explain: 교수진은 한 학교나 학과의 교수들을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이라 한 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 그 사람은 '교수님'이라고 불러요. 학원이나 병원처럼 가르치거나 치료하는 사람들의 팀은 '강사진', '의료진'처럼 '-진'을 붙여요.

phrases.en: This university is famous for its excellent faculty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교를 칭찬할 때 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together when praising a school.

phrases.en: This academy has good instructors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교수진은 대학, 강사진은 학원 같은 곳에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '교수진' is for universities; '강사진' for academies and the like.

phrases.example: 학교 홈페이지에서 교수진 소개를 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can see the faculty introductions on the school website.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 학과의 교수들을 안내하는 글이나 화면에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on pages that introduce a school's or department's professors.

explain_en: 교수진 refers to all professors of a school or department together, so you don't use it for one person, who is addressed as '교수님'. The suffix '-진' also makes words for other groups, such as '강사진' (instructors) and '의료진' (medical staff).

examples.en: I get along well with my classmates.
I finished my homework with a classmate's help.

examples.ko: 급우 중에 노래를 잘하는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: Among my classmates, there is a friend who sings well.
I quickly became close with my new classmate.

examples.ko: 급우 한 명이 전학을 가서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: One classmate transferred to another school, which is a pity.
The teacher told us to help our classmates.

explain: 같은 반 친구를 뜻하지만 글이나 공식적인 말에서 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '반 친구'라고 말하는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I eat lunch with a classmate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급우'와 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 급우 but more natural in everyday talk.

phrases.en: All my classmates clapped.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 명의 같은 반 친구를 말해요. 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -들 makes it plural; common in writing.

phrases.en: The classmates in our class get along well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 반 친구들 사이의 관계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about relationships among classmates.

explain_en: Somewhat formal/written — students in the same class (급우들) It means a classmate but is mostly used in writing or formal speech. In everyday conversation, '반 친구' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I get along well with my classmates.

en: to be warm-hearted; to be affectionate; to be tender

examples.ko: 우리 담임 선생님은 다정다감해서 학생들이 좋아해요.
examples.en: Our homeroom teacher is warm and tender, so the students like her.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 겉으로는 무뚝뚝해도 속은 다정다감해요.
examples.en: He looks gruff on the outside, but he's tender inside.

examples.ko: 다정다감한 아버지 덕분에 저는 편하게 자랐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my tender-hearted father, I grew up comfortably.

examples.ko: 남편이 다정다감하게 안부를 물어 줘서 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was grateful that my husband asked after me so warmly.
When I was little, my grandmother was always warm and tender.
I'm not a tender person, so I'm clumsy at showing feelings.

explain: '다정하다'와 비슷한데, 마음이 따뜻할 뿐 아니라 감정이 풍부하고 정이 많은 사람에게 써요. 주로 사람의 성격을 말할 때 나와요. 반대로는 '무뚝뚝하다'를 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My older sister is a warm-hearted person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for describing a person's personality.

phrases.en: My father is warm and affectionate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 사람의 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for describing someone's character.

phrases.en: That teacher is very kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이 풍부하다는 느낌이 없이 따뜻하고 친절하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means warm and kind, without the sense of rich emotion.

explain_en: Warm, gentle and attentive toward people close to you. It is close to '다정하다', but it describes someone who is not only kind but also rich in feeling and affection. It is mostly used for a person's character. A common opposite is '무뚝뚝하다'.

examples.en: I decided to go to the high school alumni meeting tomorrow.
I met my seniors after a long time at the alumni meeting.

examples.ko: 동문회 회장님이 모임 장소를 정해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The president of the alumni association chose the meeting place.
Our school's alumni association collected scholarship money.
The alumni meeting is held every autumn.
I was introduced to a good job through the alumni association.

explain: 같은 학교를 졸업한 사람들의 모임이에요. '동창회'는 같은 해에 졸업한 친구들의 모임으로 많이 쓰고, 동문회는 선배와 후배까지 같은 학교 출신이 모두 모이는 모임으로 많이 써요. '서울대 동문회'처럼 학교 이름을 앞에 붙여요.

phrases.en: We hold an alumni gathering every year after graduation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임을 한다고 말할 때 '열다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '열다' to say the gathering is held.

phrases.en: I am a member of my university alumni association.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 속한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people who belong to the association.

phrases.en: I have a middle school class reunion tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 해에 졸업한 친구들의 모임에 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more for gatherings of friends who graduated in the same year.

explain_en: It is a gathering of people who graduated from the same school. 동창회 is mostly used for friends who graduated the same year, while 동문회 is mostly used for everyone from the same school, including seniors and juniors. The school name goes in front, like '서울대 동문회'.

examples.ko: 자동차 딜러가 차 종류를 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The car dealer explained the types of cars.
I met a dealer because I wanted to buy a new car.
I asked the dealer to lower the price.

examples.ko: 외환 딜러는 하루 종일 화면을 봐요.
examples.en: A foreign exchange dealer watches the screen all day.
I signed the car contract after talking with the dealer.
I have a friend who works as a dealer.

explain: 딜러는 앞에 말을 붙여서 어떤 일을 하는지 말해요. '자동차 딜러', '외환 딜러'처럼요. 물건이 아니라 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.

phrases.en: A foreign exchange dealer keeps checking exchange rates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국 돈을 사고파는 일을 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who buys and sells foreign currency.

phrases.en: I asked the used car dealer about the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중고차를 파는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who sells used cars.

phrases.en: Please ask the dealer if you're curious about something.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에게'를 붙여서 딜러를 대상으로 한 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-에게' marks the dealer as the person you ask.

explain_en: 딜러 takes a word in front to say what the person deals in, as in '자동차 딜러' and '외환 딜러'. It refers to a person, not a thing.

examples.en: An Olympic medalist came to our school to give a talk.
That athlete is a medalist at a world championship.
The three medalists stepped onto the podium.

examples.ko: 저는 메달리스트를 꿈꾸며 매일 새벽에 훈련해요.
examples.en: I train every dawn, dreaming of becoming a medalist.
I saw a medalist's interview on the news yesterday.
There is prize money for the medalists of this competition.

explain: '금메달리스트', '은메달리스트', '동메달리스트'처럼 앞에 색을 붙여 써요. 메달을 땄다는 말은 '메달을 따다'라고 해요. 뉴스와 스포츠 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That swimmer is a gold medalist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금메달을 딴 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who won a gold medal.

phrases.en: The bronze medalist also received big applause.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동메달을 딴 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who won a bronze medal.

phrases.en: A Korean athlete won a medal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메달을 받게 되었다는 뜻으로 '따다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '따다' is the verb used for winning a medal.

explain_en: You can put the color in front, as in '금메달리스트', '은메달리스트' and '동메달리스트'. Winning a medal is said '메달을 따다'. It often appears in news and sports talk.

en: to be considerate of; to show consideration for; to act thoughtfully

examples.en: I walked slowly out of consideration for my friend.
If we are considerate of each other, there is nothing to fight about.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 다른 사람을 배려하는 편이에요.
examples.en: That person tends to always think of others.
It was a considerate thing to say, so it felt good.

examples.ko: 아이를 배려하지 않은 행동에 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I was angry at the behavior that showed no thought for the child.
I will be more considerate from now on.

explain: 명사로는 '배려가 깊다', '배려심이 있다'처럼 써요. '신경 쓰다'는 더 가볍게 쓰고, '배려하다'는 상대 입장을 생각해서 행동한다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: That friend is very considerate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 생각하는 마음을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for a thoughtful, caring mind.

phrases.en: The teacher is deeply thoughtful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '배려'에 형용사를 붙여 말하는 방식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the noun 배려 with an adjective.

phrases.en: The teacher was considerate of me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙여 상대를 위해 해 준다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 주다 shows doing it for someone else.

explain_en: Thoughtful care for another person's feelings or needs. The noun appears in '배려가 깊다' (very considerate) and '배려심이 있다' (have a considerate heart). '신경 쓰다' (pay attention) is lighter, while '배려하다' suggests acting from the other person's point of view.

t90.ax: I will be more considerate from now on.

examples.en: The child grew up under his grandmother's care.

examples.ko: 이 아기 고양이는 보살핌이 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: This kitten needs a lot of care.
I was grateful to receive warm care at the hospital.
Even a potted plant withers quickly without care.
For older people, family care and attention are important.
Thanks to my parents' care, I became healthy.

explain: '돌봄'은 돌보는 일 자체를 말하고, 보살핌은 받는 쪽에서 더 자주 써요. '보살핌을 받다', '보살핌이 필요하다'가 자연스러워요. 하는 쪽은 '보살피다', '돌보다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The baby is cared for by its mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보살핌은 받는 쪽에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This word is often used from the receiving side.

phrases.example: 따뜻한 보살핌 덕분에 병이 빨리 나았어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the warm care, I got better quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정성스럽게 돌봐 주는 마음을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes caring that comes from the heart.

phrases.en: I look after my younger sibling every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌보는 쪽에서 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb used from the side of the caregiver.

explain_en: 돌봄 names the act of caring itself, while 보살핌 is used more from the side of the person being cared for. 보살핌을 받다 and 보살핌이 필요하다 sound natural. The person giving care says 보살피다 or 돌보다.

t90.ax: This kitten needs a lot of care.

examples.en: I'm a freshman at university this year.
I met the seniors at the freshman welcome party.

examples.ko: 회사에 들어온 새내기 직원이 열심히 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: The new employee who joined the company is learning hard.
When I was a freshman, everything felt new and exciting.

examples.ko: 새내기들은 아직 학교 건물을 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: The freshmen don't know the school buildings well yet.
The political newcomer gave his first speech.

explain: 새로 들어온 사람, 특히 대학 1학년을 친근하게 부르는 말이에요. 순우리말이라 느낌이 부드럽고, 같은 뜻의 '신입생'은 학교가 정한 공식적인 말이에요. 회사에서는 '신입 사원'이라고 하고 '새내기'는 가볍게 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: A welcome party for new students was held.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 정한 공식적인 말이에요. '새내기'는 더 친근해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official school term. 새내기 is friendlier.

phrases.en: I became a new employee this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서는 '새내기'보다 '신입 사원'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: At a company, people say 신입 사원 rather than 새내기.

phrases.en: In my freshman days, everything was new.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학 1학년 때를 친근하게 떠올릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to fondly recall one's first year of college.

explain_en: Native word for new university student; friendly, campus. 새내기 is a friendly word for someone new, especially a first-year university student. It is a native Korean word with a soft feel, whereas 신입생 is the official term. At work the formal term is 신입 사원, with 새내기 used more lightly.

t90.ax: I'm a freshman at university this year.

examples.en: The captain docked the big ship at the port.
When the storm came, the captain called everyone.
When I was little, I dreamed of being a ship captain.
I greeted the captain and boarded the ship.

examples.ko: 이 배의 선장과 이야기해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to talk with the captain of this ship.

examples.ko: 오랜 경력의 선장에게 바다 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard sea stories from a veteran captain.

explain: 배의 책임자예요. 비행기의 책임자는 '기장', 군함의 지휘관은 '함장'이라고 불러요. 높여 부를 때는 '선장님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Captain, shall we leave soon?
phrases.nuance_ko: 선장을 높여 직접 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful way to address a ship's captain directly.

phrases.example: 저는 어른이 되면 선장이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: When I grow up, I want to become a captain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for talking about dreams or jobs.

phrases.en: The captain and the crew boarded the ship together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배에서 일하는 사람들을 함께 말할 때 자주 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together to talk about the people working on a ship.

explain_en: Captain of an ordinary ship. The person in charge of a ship. The person in charge of a plane is '기장', and a warship commander is '함장'. To address one politely, say '선장님'.

examples.en: The newborn sleeps all day long.
My sister held a newborn for the first time.

examples.ko: 병원에는 신생아 전용 방이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital has a separate room just for newborns.
Newborns need a quiet environment.

examples.ko: 어제 우리 동네에서 신생아 세 명이 태어났대요.
examples.en: I heard three newborns were born in our neighborhood yesterday.
Newborn clothes are very small and soft.

explain: 갓 태어난 아기를 말할 때 '신생아'는 병원이나 뉴스처럼 조금 공식적인 자리에서 많이 써요. 가족끼리는 그냥 '아기'라고 하고, '갓난아기'는 더 부드럽고 친근하게 들려요.

phrases.en: I saw the babies in the hospital nursery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 갓 태어난 아기들이 있는 방이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The room in a hospital where newborn babies stay.

phrases.en: My younger brother was really tiny as a newborn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 갓 태어났을 때를 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Talks about the time right after a baby is born.

phrases.en: The newborn baby is sleeping in its mother's arms.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신생아'와 같은 뜻이지만 더 부드럽고 친근해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 신생아 but softer and friendlier.

explain_en: Neutral, medical or official term for a baby in its first weeks. 신생아 is the word you hear in hospitals and the news for a baby just born. Within the family people just say '아기', and '갓난아기' sounds softer and warmer.

t90.ax: The newborn sleeps all day long.

examples.ko: 앞사람 머리 때문에 영화 화면이 안 보여요.
examples.en: I can't see the movie screen because of the head of the person in front of me.
The person ahead stopped suddenly and I almost bumped into them.

examples.ko: 줄을 설 때는 앞사람과 거리를 두세요.
examples.en: When standing in line, keep some distance from the person in front.
I followed the person ahead and walked in slowly.
After the person ahead got off, I sat down.
When the person before me finishes talking, I'll ask my question too.

explain: 줄이나 자리, 순서에서 바로 앞에 있는 사람을 말하고, 반대말은 '뒷사람'이에요. 보통 줄 서기, 극장 좌석, 발표 순서 같은 상황에서 써요.

phrases.en: I didn't know the way, so I followed the person ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 앞에 가는 사람 뒤에서 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving behind the person right in front.

phrases.example: 산길에서는 앞사람과 거리를 두고 천천히 걸으세요.
phrases.en: On mountain trails, keep some distance from the person ahead and walk slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄을 서거나 걸을 때 앞사람과 간격을 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for keeping space from the person in front, in line or while walking.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep distance from the person ahead

phrases.en: The person ahead stood up and I can't see the screen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 극장이나 공연장 좌석에서 자주 나오는 상황이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common situation in theaters or concert halls.

explain_en: Person ahead of you in a line or order, neutral. It means the person right in front of you in a line, seat or order, and the opposite is '뒷사람'. It typically comes up in situations like queuing, theater seats and speaking order.

examples.en: The heroine of this drama is a brave nurse.

examples.ko: 여주인공이 눈물을 흘리는 장면에서 저도 울었어요.
examples.en: I cried too in the scene where the heroine sheds tears.

examples.ko: 새 영화에서 유명한 배우가 여주인공을 맡았어요.
examples.en: A famous actress took the female lead in the new movie.
I was drawn to the heroine of the novel.

examples.ko: 여주인공과 남자 주인공이 처음 만나는 장면이 재미있어요.
examples.en: The scene where the heroine and hero first meet is fun.

examples.ko: 저는 여주인공 역할을 꼭 해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to try playing the female lead.

explain: 이야기에서 중심이 되는 여자 인물이에요. 남자는 '남자 주인공'이라고 하고, 성별 구분 없이는 그냥 '주인공'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The female lead is really pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여주인공'과 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 풀어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '여주인공', just spelled out in full.

phrases.en: That actor played the female lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 드라마에서 배우가 역할을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an actor taking a role in a film or drama.

phrases.example: 오늘은 제가 이야기의 여주인공이 된 기분이에요.
phrases.en: Today I feel like the heroine of a story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 그런 기분이 들 때도 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used figuratively when you feel like the star.

explain_en: Main female character in a drama, film or novel. This is the central female character in a story. The male counterpart is 남자 주인공, and the plain word 주인공 works with no gender.
